A weight-norm scan would never have found them; their large activation must come from the inputs they receive in chat-format math. To see whether 6176 is the first stage of a longer circuit, I'll look downstream. For each later layer (12–25), I'll take the gate_proj and up_proj rows, scaled by that layer's pre_feedforward_layernorm weight (Gemma applies 1+w), and find the neurons whose input rows align best with neuron 6176's down vector (after layer 11's post_feedforward_layernorm scaling). Then I'll check, with fwd_14 statistics, whether those top readers are also math-selective. A reader with high alignment that is strongly math-on would extend the circuit, giving more components to ablate and a stronger mechanistic case. If the top readers are not math-selective, 6176's effect is diffuse.

Its effect, if real, is distributed rather than a clean two-stage circuit. The most important open question is whether the +4.7 gain from zeroing is real or noise (1.9 SE), and the monotone response (zero helps, reverse hurts) makes it worth confirming. I'll restore E4 exactly (zero layer-11 down_proj columns 6176 and 6508), save a copy to /work/best_1, and run "both" on the other DEV half, dev_b[256:512]. So I'll look for other units with the same AND signature in layers 2–17; the late layers were already checked in fwd_10 and showed no switches.
